newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai sends first container ship to Iraq since 1981.
newsitem.headline: Dubai sends first container ship to Iraq since 1981.

text.p: A Dubai-based shipping company has launched the first container service to Iraq since just after Iraq's eight-year war with Iran broke out in 1981, the firm's managing director said on Sunday.
Mohammad Maghami of Simatech Shipping and Forwarding Company said a vessel carrying 2,500 tonnes of vegetable oil left Dubai on the two-day trip to Iraq's southern Umm Qasr port on Saturday.

The consignment on the Perma Glory, authorised by the United Nations which imposed a trade embargo on Iraq after it invaded Kuwait in August 1990, was brought to Dubai from Malaysia by Uniglory, a Taiwan-based operator.
"The Perma Glory will be the first international cargo container vessel to call on Umm Qasr since 1981," Maghami told Reuters.
Shippers in Dubai, the Gulf's trade and service centre, said they wanted to handle more Iraqi trade with Asia, which currently goes through Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.
Operators said they were waiting to see conditions at Umm Qasr and how long it would take the vessel to unload before deciding on the next move.
"Big operators are not clear how things will work in Iraq and Perma Glory might open the door for them to follow suit and resume their services," one shipping executive said.
Facilities at Umm Qasr and nearby Khour al-Zubair have not been modernised since Iraq's war with Iran. Large vessels cannot reach them because harbours are too shallow.
Maghami said Simatech hoped to offer weekly sailings from Dubai, depending on the turnaround time and U.N. inspections of the cargo at sea.
"Everything mostly depends on the Iraqi side being able to utilise their equipment to handle goods," he said.
